Fixture brief for stare's golden tests. The citations resolve against the fixture
mirror in tests/common; the propositions are invented.

Id. at 5. A residence, not a mailing address, is the test of domicile. D'Elia & Marks
Co. v. Lyon, 31 A.2d 647 (D.C. Mun. Ct. App. 1943). Id. at 648. The rule was applied in
Waterman v. Railway Express Agency, 31 A.2d 657 (D.C. Mun. Ct. App. 1943), and in
Brooks v. District of Columbia, 31 A.2d 657 (1943). See also 31 A.2d 650; 31 A.2d 659.
D'Elia, 31 A.2d at 649. Waterman, supra, at 658.

The same case in another reporter: Pettegrew v. Pettegrew, 128 Neb. 783, 260 N.W. 287
(1935). Printings that disagree: Smith v. Jones, 250 A.3d 100, 31 A.2d 660 (Pa. 2021).

Records from CourtListener: In re Doe, 2021 NY Slip Op 01234. See Doe v. United
States, 10 F.4th 100 (2d Cir. 2021). See also Roe v. Commissioner, T.C. Memo. 2019-123.
State v. Roe, 2019-Ohio-1234. A page with no case: 250 A.3d 101. Elsewhere: Roe v.
Wade, 410 U.S. 113 (1973).

Statutes: 42 U.S.C. § 1983; Conn. Gen. Stat. § 52-584; Minn. Stat. § 609.185. Id.
